solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kind enough to study team and make an assessment

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over, as in conning a text
a side is a team in sport
to rate something is to assess or value it

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtful enough to look at a squad closely and judge it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enough to' and 'and' are link words between the definition and the three charade pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thoughtful of others is a synonym for being kind, which is what considerate means.

clue.text: Finished in a superior position

definitions.meaning: a thing that is done and ended is said to be ...
... also means above or higher up

explanation.definitionFit: Over means both ended, as in 'the game is over', and placed above something else.

clue.text: Vessel for the Sunday joint

parts.note: reads like a dish for the roast, but the vessel is a seagoing one and a 'joint' is slang for a pub, many of which bear this vessel's name

explanation.surface: A roasting dish needed to cook the traditional Sunday roast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the 'Sunday joint' is the weekly roast meat; here 'joint' is the slang sense of a drinking place, and 'vessel' a boat rather than a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a general word for a boat, of which this is the commonest everyday example.

clue.text: A second order of clergy

indicators.note: putting letters in a new order signals that the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rank of churchmen ranking just below the priests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order of clergy' reads as one phrase about church ranks, but 'order of' is the anagram signal on A SECOND, and 'clergy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Deacons are ordained ministers, so they are members of the clergy.

clue.text: It's used in casting part of a film

definitions.meaning: an angler casts a line wound on a spool fixed to the rod
a cinema film was supplied on several spools, each one a section of the whole

explanation.definitionFit: A reel is both the angler's line winder and one spool-length section of a movie.

clue.text: College threesome

definitions.meaning: The name of colleges at Cambridge, Oxford and Dublin
a group of three

explanation.definitionFit: The word names famous university colleges and also means a group of three.

clue.text: Minimum investment for patrons of the pools

definitions.text: Minimum investment for patrons of the pools

parts.words: Minimum investment for patrons of the pools
parts.note: sounds like the smallest stake for those who bet on the football pools, but to invest is also to clothe, so it is the least clothing worn by swimmers

explanation.surface: The smallest stake allowed for people who play the football pools.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a British betting game on match results; 'investment' is read in its old sense of dressing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimwear is the bare minimum of clothing worn by people at swimming pools.

clue.text: Poor little creature

parts.note: sounds like pity for a small animal, but alludes to the saying 'as poor as' this rodent living in a place of worship

explanation.surface: An expression of sympathy for a small, pitiable animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'as poor as a church mouse' means having no money at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial mouse living in a church is the byword for being penniless.

clue.text: A symptom of fever like a hot head

definitions.meaning: a skin eruption that comes with many fevers
a hothead acts hastily and without thought

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a skin eruption and an adjective meaning hasty or reckless.

clue.text: Precipitate action for itinerant

indicators.note: putting the letters into action, set to work, signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hasty measure taken on behalf of a wandering traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action for' joins the anagram signal to the definition: PRECIPITATE rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerant and peripatetic are synonyms, both describing someone who travels from place to place.

clue.text: A cleaner cup is needed to hold it

definitions.meaning: a charwoman is a cleaning lady

definitions.text: cup is needed to hold it
definitions.meaning: British slang for tea, which is drunk from a cup

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman needs a cup for her tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is a link word. CHAR is everyday British slang for tea, from the Chinese word cha.
explanation.definitionFit: A char is a cleaning woman, and char is also slang for tea, drink served in a cup.

clue.text: Eating habits

parts.note: sounds like the way someone eats, but a habit is also a garment, so these are clothes worn for a formal meal

explanation.definitionFit: Formal evening wear for a meal is clothing, or habits, worn for eating.

clue.text: They will be opened for those that are late

definitions.text: They will be opened for those that are late

parts.words: They will be opened for those that are late
parts.note: sounds like doors held open for latecomers, but 'the late' are the dead, admitted to heaven

explanation.surface: Doors are kept unlocked for people who arrive late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means deceased, as in 'the late king'; the entrance to heaven is said to be guarded by St Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: In tradition the entrance to heaven is a set of gates made of pearl, through which the dead pass.

clue.text: Country music composer

definitions.meaning: a nation in north-west Europe
John ... was an English composer of the twentieth century

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a nation's name and the surname of the English composer John Ireland.

clue.text: One sings his praises

parts.note: sounds like a flatterer, but the praises are the psalms, songs of praise attributed to a biblical king

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps praising a particular man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his praises' means praises he wrote: the biblical psalms are traditionally credited to King David.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical king is credited with the psalms, songs of praise still sung in church.

clue.text: Stay true

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, especially of blood
loyal and steadfast

explanation.definitionFit: Staunch is a verb meaning to stop a flow and an adjective meaning loyal or faithful.

clue.text: Like a judge with robes in disarray

indicators.note: in a muddle or untidy state, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A judge whose official robes are messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. The phrase 'sober as a judge' supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as sober as a judge' makes a judge the type of seriousness and sobriety.

clue.text: A green and mountainous part of France

definitions.meaning: a variety of crinkly-leaved cabbage
a historical Alpine region in the south-east of France

explanation.definitionFit: Savoy names a crinkly cabbage, a green vegetable, and the Alpine region of France.

clue.text: Standard feature of Saturn or Mars

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A characteristic common to the planets Saturn and Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a usual pattern or benchmark, which is a synonym of standard.

clue.text: Consequently return to see the capital

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: so means therefore or consequently
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: As a result one goes back to visit the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'the' are link words; 'return' turns SO into OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Director gets me in tune

indicators.note: in places one word inside another word

parts.note: an air is a melody or tune
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film director finds himself singing along to a melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who aims or points something directs it, so the word means a director.

clue.text: The pile some workers make

parts.note: sounds like money earned by labourers, but the workers are insects building a mound

explanation.surface: The fortune that certain labourers manage to earn.
explanation.walkthrough: Worker ants are the ones that build the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of earth built by insect workers is their nest.

clue.text: A political favour?

parts.note: sounds like a corrupt kindness, but a favour is also a ribbon badge, worn at elections to show party support

explanation.surface: A good turn done in return for political support.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'favour' in the old sense is a ribbon or badge worn to show allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon badge worn by election candidates and supporters is a political favour.

clue.text: He's right to take Monday off

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of the day are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man is entitled to take a day off at the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link word; 'off' rearranges MONDAY into AYMOND. 'He's' defines a man's name, read as 'he is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond is a man's first name, so the clue's 'he' can be read as this man.

clue.text: Din subsides once these are ejected

definitions.text: Din subsides once these are ejected

parts.note: a row is a loud noise
to die down is to subside, so dies means subsides

explanation.surface: The noise calms down after the troublemakers are thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and the first two words build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When unruly people are thrown out, the noise they made fades away, exactly as the clue says.

clue.text: State university bowler suffers reverse

indicators.note: a reverse turns the word back to front

parts.note: a bowler is a hat

explanation.surface: A college cricket bowler has a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket but is the round hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Caledonian company in a small way

indicators.note: in places one word inside another word

parts.note: ST is the short form of street, a kind of way

explanation.surface: A Scottish firm working in a modest manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link word; 'small' signals the abbreviation of street.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a person from there.

clue.text: Assistance for the man with a record

parts.note: he refers to a man
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Support offered to a man who has a criminal record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Help and assistance are synonyms for aid given to someone.

clue.text: Cork tip

definitions.meaning: a stopper for a barrel
a bribe or payment slipped to someone

explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a stopper for a cask, and in British slang a tip or bribe.

clue.text: Coshed quite badly in the dance hall

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was violently beaten up at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is a link; 'badly' rearranges COSHED QUITE. A cosh is a British word for a club or blunt weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a nightclub where people dance, so a dance hall.

clue.text: English flower seen on the golf course

definitions.meaning: a flower is a river, something that flows
small pegs on which a golf ball is placed

explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is an English river, and tees are the pegs used to start golf holes.

clue.text: Clippers of the line?

parts.note: sounds like fast sailing ships or a shipping line, but these clip washing onto a line

explanation.surface: Fast sailing ships belonging to a shipping company.
explanation.walkthrough: Clippers were fast sailing ships, and a line is a shipping company; here they grip laundry on a clothes line.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundry pegs clip garments to a washing line to dry.
